articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo expanded his hotel empire with a €60 million Paris project featuring 210 rooms and a 2027 opening
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo's ambitions had stretched far beyond the football pitch, and his growing hotel business offered a clear example.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo's ambitions had stretched far beyond the football pitch, and his growing hotel business offered a clear example. While the Portuguese superstar continued his playing career, his Pestana CR7 brand had already established a presence in five major destinations. Its next expansion was planned for Paris, where a €60 million hotel project was expected to bring another high-profile property into the portfolio in 2027. The development also showed how Ronaldo had turned his global sporting fame into a long-term business venture, one that did not depend entirely on his performances or playing career.Cristiano Ronaldo's Pestana CR7 hotel empire had reached five destinationsRonaldo's hotel partnership with Portugal's Pestana Hotel Group began in 2015. The first Pestana CR7 property opened in Funchal, Madeira, in 2016, close to the footballer's hometown. A Lisbon hotel followed in the same year, giving the brand its first two locations.The business later expanded beyond Portugal. Properties opened in Madrid and New York in 2021, followed by Marrakech in 2022. By 2026, the partnership had five operating hotels across four destinations: Funchal, Lisbon, Madrid, New York and Marrakech.The venture was structured as a 50-50 partnership between Ronaldo and the Pestana Group. While the footballer brought his CR7 identity, public profile and investment to the project, Pestana handled the hotel operations and management.That arrangement allowed Ronaldo to take part in the hospitality business without having to manage its daily operations himself. It also helped the brand reach travellers looking for modern city hotels with a strong sports and lifestyle identity.Paris hotel project added a €60 million expansion to Ronaldo's portfolioThe planned Paris property represented the next major step for Pestana CR7. The hotel was expected to become the brand's sixth location when it opened in 2027.The development was part of the Austerlitz A7/A8 project in the French capital, near Gare d'Austerlitz. It was designed as a four-star property with 210 rooms, making it the largest hotel in the CR7 collection by room capacity.The €60 million project was also expected to feature a landscaped rooftop, a swimming pool and a bar open to the public. Its location in Paris offered the brand access to one of the world's most visited cities and a major international tourism market.The expansion came as the Pestana CR7 partnership marked its 10th anniversary in 2026. What began with a single hotel in Madeira had developed into an international hospitality brand.For Ronaldo, the Paris project added another long-term commercial venture to a portfolio that had grown well beyond football. articles.title: WTA Finals 2026: Mirra Andreeva and Elina Svitolina contest final in repeat of round-robin match
articles.summary: As the WTA Finals prepares for its next chapter, this year’s has almost been written. After an early end to the deal to host its flagship event in Riyadh, Sa...
articles.body:
As the WTA Finals prepares for its next chapter, this year's has almost been written.

After an early end to the deal to host its flagship event in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, the WTA is stopping off at Indian Wells, Calif ., before a three-year run in Charlotte, N.C . Over those four editions, the governing body intends to restore its flagship event's status and relevance, starting this November in the Coachella Valley.

The eight best singles players and doubles pairs of the season compete. The tournament was set to be headlined by the new world No. 1, Elena Rybakina , and the player she dethroned, world No. 2 Aryna Sabalenka . But Rybakina, this year's Australian Open and U.S. Open champion, withdrew due to a viral illness on the eve of the tournament . Sabalenka, who lost to Rybakina in both of those Grand Slam finals, will look to make a statement heading into 2027.

French Open champion Mirra Andreeva and Wimbledon champion and finalist, Linda Nosková and Karolína Muchová, made their debuts at the event. Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula of the U.S. return and Ukraine's Elina Svitolina looks to cap her best season in a long time. She was ultimately joined by compatriot Marta Kostyuk, who replaces Rybakina as an alternate.

Here's everything you need to know about the tournament, with the schedule and results updated day by day.

Who is in the WTA Finals championship match for 2026?

The singles semifinals pitted Jessica Pegula against Mirra Andreeva and Elina Svitolina against Linda Nosková.

Svitolina had stunned Aryna Sabalenka to seal a place in the last four, while Pegula knocked out Coco Gauff by defeating Nosková. Pegula and Andreeva will meet for the first time, after a hot mic caught Pegula's labeling Andreeva a "diva " before the start of the tournament. The duo has since laughed it off.

It was Andreeva who prevailed in their first meeting, winning 6-3, 6-4 in a scratchy match to reach the final on her tournament debut. She will meet Svitolina in the final, after the Ukrainian rolled past a flat Linda Nosková 6-2, 6-1 in just 64 minutes.

The wins mean that Andreeva has dropped the fewest games (18) of any player en route to the final since the round-robin format was introduced in 2003. Svitolina, meanwhile, now has more top-10 wins this year than any other player on the WTA Tour, with 11.

The eight players who qualified were split into four pots for the draw. Pot 1 is No. 1 and No. 2, Pot 2 is No. 3 and No. 4, and so on.

These seedings follow the players' rankings in the WTA Race , a table that counts only ranking points earned in 2026.

Each player then plays three round-robin matches. The top two players from each group contest the semifinals, with the winners meeting in the final.

On Nov. 14, it is semifinal day, with singles again followed by doubles and play again starting at 12 p.m. PT. The finals follow the same schedule on Nov. 15.

Rybakina won the singles title at the 2025 WTA Finals , held in Riyadh. She defeated Sabalenka 6-3, 7-6(0) in the final, winning all five of her matches at the event. The title earned Rybakina the largest winner's check in women's sports history, at $5,235,000.

In the doubles, Russia's Veronika Kudermetova and Belgium's Elise Mertens defeated Hungary's Tímea Babos and Brazil's Luisa Stefani in the final, 7-6(4), 6-1. They split just over $1 million.

What is the prize money for the 2026 WTA Finals?

This year's prize pool is $10 million, with $8 million for the singles competition and $2 million. It is allocated per match win and structured so the singles champion takes home the biggest prize if they go through the event undefeated with five wins (three round-robin wins, a semifinal win, and then victory in the final).

Last year's prize pool was $15.5 million.

The winner of the singles final will receive $3.37 million, while the winner of each semifinal will receive $820,000; the prize for a round-robin match win is $230,000 and each singles player receives $220,000 just for appearing at the event, provided that they play all three of their round-robin matches.

The winning doubles pair will receive $725,000 if they go undefeated.

What ranking points do the players receive?

Round-robin wins carry 200 points, a semifinal win carries 400 points and a final win carries 500 points. An undefeated champion (three round-robin wins, a semifinal win and a final win) will earn 1,500 points.

Saudi Arabia's sports ministry and the Saudi Tennis Federation completed a three-year deal for the WTA Finals in April 2024. Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund already sponsored the ATP and WTA world rankings, and this deal was the biggest element of the kingdom's push into tennis before it announced an ATP Masters 1000 tournament that will start as early as 2028.

That deal ended a year early, in part because of the Iran conflict but also because the WTA Finals had outlived its usefulness to Saudi Arabia's wider tennis ambitions , two people briefed on its sports ministry's operations, speaking on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly, said.

"We have an incredible opportunity to bring the WTA Finals, a world-class, premium global event showcasing the best in women's tennis, to a new home," a spokesperson for the WTA said in a statement following the announcement of the early departure from Saudi Arabia.

That departure left the WTA Tour in need of a venue for 2026, and it alighted on Indian Wells, where the prestigious ATP Masters 1000 and WTA 1000 event is held each March. From 2027, the WTA Finals will be held in Charlotte, N.C., for at least three years.

articles.title: Waddles’ 30 lead Campbell over South Carolina Upstate 93-77
articles.summary: (AP) — Lance Waddles’ 30 points led Campbell over South Carolina Upstate 93-77 on Saturday.Waddles added five rebounds for the Fighting Camels (1-3).
articles.body:
BUIES CREEK, N.C. (AP) — Lance Waddles' 30 points led Campbell over South Carolina Upstate 93-77 on Saturday.

Waddles added five rebounds for the Fighting Camels (1-3). Nordin Kapic scored 17 points while going 7 of 8 (2 for 3 from 3-point range), and added five rebounds and six assists. Rashawn Inglemon shot 5 for 13, including 4 for 9 from beyond the arc to finish with 14 points, while adding five assists and four steals.

Jalyn Patterson finished with 25 points for the Spartans (1-4). South Carolina Upstate also got 16 points from Ries Naugle. David Tubek finished with 11 points.

Campbell took the lead for good with 17:54 left in the first half. The score was 44-30 at halftime, with Waddles racking up 20 points. Campbell outscored South Carolina Upstate by two points over the final half, while Karim Rtail led the way with a team-high 14 second-half points.

articles.title: Braves Bullpen Moves Signal Iggy Is Back, But Red Sox Are In Trouble
articles.summary: The Braves are doubling down on Raisel Iglesias while the Red Sox face a messy decision with Kristian Campbell. Here is why the moves matter for the NL East.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Braves are wasting time circling veteran closer Raisel Iglesias again. After re-signing him for one year and $16 million just last offseason, the team is still hunting for the same arm. MLB Trade Rumors reports that Atlanta and Detroit remain interested in the 36-year-old righty even after adding other relievers. This feels like a bad habit. Teams that chase aging closers often end up with a broken bullpen and no depth. The Braves should look elsewhere for their late-inning help.

Washington Is Playing Chess While Atlanta Plays Checkers

While Atlanta chases one name, the Washington Nationals are actually building a real plan. The team had one of the worst bullpens in baseball in 2026, yet they are being smart about the fix. According to reports, relievers requiring multi-year deals and substantial salaries are likely unavailable to D.C., a sound decision for a club that secured 77 victories during its rebuild. They know they cannot just throw big cash at free agents.

Instead of spending big on one guy, the Nationals are hunting for starting pitching. Spencer Nusbaum reports that the Nats have inquired regarding controllable starting pitching in trade discussions and are exploring more options than they did last season. They also hired John Morris as their new VP of baseball research to lead the analytics side. Morris comes from the Yankees, where he was the assistant director of quantitative analysis.

The Marlins Move Thompson to the Front Office

The Miami Marlins made a solid hire by bringing Trayce Thompson into their baseball operations department. Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports the news, which likely signals the end of Thompson's playing career. Between 2015 and 2023, this 35-year-old competed in segments of seven MLB seasons. After representing Great Britain, he finished his career with three seasons in the minors, the Mexican League, and independent baseball.

Thompson ended his career boasting 45 homers and a .212/.300/.411 slash line across 1,058 plate appearances. His best stretch came in the second half of 2022 with the Dodgers. Moving a former player into an operations role makes sense.

articles.title: Auburn Football Becomes Bowl Eligible With Dominant 41-9 Win Over Mississippi State
articles.summary: The Auburn Tigers are bowl-eligible in Alex Golesh's first season after dominating Mississippi State 41-9 in Starkville. Byrum Brown led the offense, Keshaun...
articles.body:
The Tigers pick up their sixth win of the season, taking down the Mississippi State Bulldogs 41-9 in Starkville on Saturday. The team capitalized on plenty of turnovers and multiple quarterbacks against the Bulldogs as they move to 4-4 in SEC play.

Here is what you need to know from the contest.

It was an overall great effort by the Tigers' defense on Saturday against Mississippi State, only holding the team to one touchdown in the contest.

The defense picked up four turnovers in the game, all coming from fumbles by Mississippi State's offense. Darrion Smith had a big breakout game with two sacks and a forced fumble.

Shadarius Toodle continued his great play s ince making his debut last week against Arkansas and led the team with 10 tackles, including 1 sack and two tackles for a loss.

Toward the end of the game, when the score was getting out of hand, Mississippi State had two drives that threatened to score a touchdown. However, DJ Durkin's defense stopped them each time on goal-line stands inside the 5-yard line.

The defensive unit played hard the entire game, even when the lead was out of reach for their opponent.

Byrum Brown had a good overall game on Saturday, controlling most of the game for Auburn and helping them pick up their sixth win of the season.

After the team's normal slow start in the first quarter, Byrum on the offense turned things around quickly with a touchdown pass to Keshaun Singleton. Singleton led the team with 7 receptions for 103 yards and 2 touchdowns in the game, including a 42-yard reception, the team's longest Catch of the year.

Arkansas has only recorded two interceptions on the entire season, and Joel Gordon allowed Byrum Brown to take deep shots, something that we haven't seen too much during the first few games of the year. The success of this explosive offense could mean a more potent side of the football for the last three games of the season.

That's right. The Auburn Tigers will play 13 games this season for the first time since 2023. With the win in Starkville, the Auburn Tigers picked up their sixth win of the year and are now bowl-eligible in the first year under Alex Golesh.

Auburn won the games they were supposed to win this season, plus stealing one in Athens against the number one team in the country, the Georgia Bulldogs. The more impressive thing is they became bowl eligible before having to play their FCS opponent, Samford, who they will take on next week at Jordan-Hare Stadium.

Barring any changes or major travel woes, next week's game is scheduled for a 2:30 pm Central kickoff and will be available on SEC Network.

articles.title: AFC Toronto downs Montreal 1-0 for the Northern Super League title
articles.summary: OTTAWA, Ontario (AP) — Teenager Olivia Chisholm scored her first goal in the 39th minute and AFC Toronto went on to win the Northern Super League's Diana B....
articles.body:
OTTAWA, Ontario (AP) — Teenager Olivia Chisholm scored her first goal in the 39th minute and AFC Toronto went on to win the Northern Super League's Diana B. Matheson Cup championship with a 1-0 victory over the Montreal Roses.

Toronto finished first in the standings last season but fell to the Vancouver Rise in the league's first championship game. This season Toronto advanced to the title game by downing Ottawa 8-2 on aggregate in the two-leg semifinals.

"I mean, obviously last year didn't go our way, so this year means so much," said Toronto midfielder Nikayla Small. "Shoutout to Olivia Chisholm for scoring that beautiful goal because that's what really got us here today."

Chisholm, 17, took a pass from Lauren Rowe and beat Roses goalkeeper Gabrielle Lambert from the middle of the box.

"I saw Lauren had the ball, and she took a bit of a bigger touch," Chisholm said. "But I know with her speed that she was going to get there, and their whole backline kind of just dropped off so I knew that the space was there for me. And as it left my foot I kind of had a good feeling that it was going to go in, and then it did."

The Roses finished atop the standings and won the Supporters Shield, riding a 12-match unbeaten streak going into the final at TD Place in Ottawa.

Montreal advanced to the final with a 5-2 victory on aggregate against Vancouver.

articles.title: Michigan football loses four-star DB commit Tavares Harrington
articles.summary: Four-star recruit Tavares Harrington flipped his commitment from Michigan to Mississippi at halftime of U-M's loss to Oregon, according to reports.
articles.body:
Michigan football didn't just lose on the field.

While t he Wolverines were losing to Oregon on Saturday, Nov. 14, in the Pacific Northwest, they suffered a loss in the Chicago area as four-star recruit Tavares Harrington flipped his commitment from Michigan to Mississippi at halftime, according to reports.

The Chicago native (Mount Carmel High School) pledged to the Wolverines in May, following in the footsteps of teammate – and four-star wide receiver – Quentin Burrell. Harrington, a 6-foot-2, 175-pound defensive back, is the No. 7 rated player in Illinois, No. 15 safety nationally and No. 124 player in the class of 2027 regardless of position, per 247 Sports' composite rankings.

Ole Miss was originally in Harrington's final four, along with Alabama and Auburn. Michigan now has four defensive backs committed for 2027, including four-star cornerback Monsanna Torbert Jr (Cincinnati), four-star cornerback Blake Jenkins (Katy, Texas), four-star cornerback Darius Johnson (Riverside, California) and three-star safety Charles Woodson Jr. (Lake Nona, Florida).

Michigan now has 22 verbal commitments in the class of 2027 ahead of the early signing period on Dec. 2-4, and its class ranks No. 17 in the country.

articles.title: 3 key stats from Indiana football’s 27-13 win over USC
articles.summary: From Khobie Martin’s running to the third down conversions, here’s some numbers that stuck out from the Hoosiers’ win.
articles.body:
Indiana football beat USC 27-13 on Saturday afternoon at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, moving to 9-1 in 2026 and earning its first ranked win of the season.

It wasn't always pretty, as it usually isn't for these Hoosiers, but it was a win, as it usually is for these Hoosiers. Indiana's defense remained as stout as ever while the offense turned things around in the second half to go up multiple scores in the fourth quarter.

Here's a few key stats that jumped off the box score:

Martin saw his first truly significant action of the 2026 season here and made the most of it, leading the Hoosiers with 82 yards on the ground with multiple explosive plays to show for it. He wasn't without help, Lee Beebe Jr. added 71 yards of his own.

But Martin found a dimension that the running game just hasn't had in weeks with his ability to plow through any gaps for bigger gains rather than a chipping away on early downs. His 37-yard run late in the third quarter to set up the go-ahead touchdown and put pressure on USC proved critical when the Trojans turned that pressure into a missed field goal to open the fourth.

Martin was always going to have a role in this backfield if he was healthy. If he's running like this? It could be a featured one.

USC was able to pick up pretty substantial chunks throughout the night, getting all the way into scoring position deep in Indiana territory before fizzling out as the Hoosier defense refused to break.

Still, it's notable that the Trojans were able to get those gains. Indiana has always been more of a bend-don't-break defense under Bryant Haines and Curt Cignetti, and break it most certainly did not, but its forced more stalled drives than that in the past.

It's very much worth noting that the Hoosiers aren't at full strength. This was A.J. Harris' first game back from injury after he bolstered the secondary earlier this season and the unit was without stalwart linebacker Rolijah Hardy entirely.

Indiana's defense played more than well enough, but 400+ yards is a considerable number.

How about this? Indiana played some of its best ball when it mattered most, going over 50% on its third down attempts on the game, including 3/4 in crunch time to help seal the game in the fourth quarter.

The name of the game here was sustained drives, something the Hoosiers haven't really had for a minute that's forced so much more game pressure on the defense. Indiana keeping things moving allowed the offense to get into position for those deep endzone shots to Charlie Becker while the defense was able to catch some much-deserved breath.

Indiana's going to have to keep that up and improve to get where the Hoosiers want to go this season.

articles.title: Georgia football plays without Drew Bobo, welcomes back Chauncey Bowens
articles.summary: Georgia football didn't have fifth-year center Drew Bobo against Missouri, but it did have junior running back Chauncey Bowens.
articles.body:
Check out our Georgia football vs. Missouri photo gallery: Best images

Georgia football played its game against Missouri on Saturday, Nov. 14, without its usual center.

Fifth year Drew Bobo was out, though head coach Kirby Smart didn't reveal the reason postgame.

"He's dealing with a little minor issue that he had during the week," Smart said. "He's had it all year. He's frustrated but hopefully getting back."

In his place, snapping to fifth year quarterback Gunner Stockton was sophomore Cortez Smith. He didn't do anything differently to earn the role over the veterans like juniors Malachi Toliver and Henry Peagler, though.

"He snapped, just like all of them," Smart said, a bit in disbelief when asked what Smith might've done to stand out. "He goes out and he works. He competes. People are going to see the five linemen, right? There's 12 other lineman that are out there going against the defense. The offense is getting better, and they don't get an opportunity to play. He was one of those guys."

Smart said Smith did everything he had to do to put him in position to go play, and that was that. He's not the only one doing that, either.

"There's a bunch of guys out there that practice every day that don't get to play," Smart said.

For the first time since the Vanderbilt game on Oct. 3, junior running back Chauncey Bowens was back on the gridiron for the No. 1 Bulldogs. He even scored a touchdown.

"He pushes every day," Smart said of Bowens. "I thought he had a better week of practice. I think he would tell you he's not at 100%, but he's pushing to go and get better. He brings a physicality to us that we really don't have. You know, that size back. But we keep wanting him to get more healthy and ... he was much closer this week than he was in previous weeks."

For reference, Bowens is listed at 5-foot-11 and 225 pounds. He is the biggest running back on the team.

Georgia (9-1) travels to South Carolina (6-3) to close out the conference slate at 7:30 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21.

articles.title: Lakers Make Decision on Austin Reaves Amid Heel Injury
articles.summary: Los Angeles Lakers guard Austin Reaves will miss Sunday's game against the Phoenix Suns due to the heel injury he sustained Wednesday. The post Lakers Make D...
articles.body:
Los Angeles Lakers guard Austin Reaves will miss Sunday's game against the Phoenix Suns due to the heel injury he sustained against the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday.

Reaves came down awkwardly on his heel in the third quarter against the Bucks, eventually leaving the game after the play ended. After the game, Reaves' x-rays came back negative, and the team opted not to undergo further testings. He didn't participate in practice on Saturday.

The guard has been one of the Lakers' most consistent players so far this season, averaging 24.7 points per game alongside 3.3 rebounds and 4.7 assists. He's shooting an efficient 51.3% from the field on the year, and is shooting 40.9% from deep, which would be the best of his career if he keeps the same form.

Reaves is one of two players who will miss the game against the Suns, as the Lakers also listed Cameron Carr as out as he deals with an illness.

Adou Thiero is questionable with a left ankle sprain, as is Bronny James with illness. Collin Sexton is also recovering from a head injury he sustained against the Bucks, but fully participated in practice on Saturday and expects to be available.

Luka Doncic, who came out of Wednesday's game in the fourth quarter with an ankle injury, is not on the injury report and will be active.

The Lakers heavily invested in their backcourt depth this offseason, so missing Reaves for a game isn't the end of the world for them. They still have Doncic running point, and have Quentin Grimes and Sexton available to fill in next to him.

Grimes has started two of his 11 games this season, making him the more likely candidate to see more time due to his absence on the injury report. He's averaging eight points per game with 2.5 rebounds and 2.5 assists on the year.

Sexton has played a valuable role for the team as well, coming off of the bench to lead the second unit, and is averaging 10.33 points and 2.6 assists per game on 17.8 minutes per night.

The Lakers are currently tied atop the Western Conference standings with the San Antonio Spurs, and will hope to pull away from them with a win over the Suns on Sunday. That won't come easily, though, as the Suns won three of five matchups against the Lakers last season.

articles.title: Match review: Spirit end Royals season in team’s first semifinal appearance
articles.summary: Cloé Lacasse’ goal was not enough as Trinity Rodman and Washington end Utah’s season
articles.body:
Utah Royals record breaking season comes to an end in the first semifinal match on Saturday following a 2-1 defeat away against the Washington Spirit.

Cloé Lacasse scored the fastest goal in NWSL playoff history with a beautiful olympico goal, coming just 117 seconds into the match. In the end it wasn't enough as the Royals season ended after reaching the semifinals for the first time in club history.

"I think the reason people are congratulating us on a season well done but we were 90 minutes away from changing the narrative and making it a better season. We didn't lose today, we won today, we came out strong at the beginning of the game and kept ourselves in it for the whole 90'." — Head coach Jimmy Coenraets on the Royals' 2026 season.

The Royals started on the front foot with an early goal off a corner kick taken by Canadian international Lacasse to give Utah the 1-0 lead two minutes in. Washington Spirit striker, Clara Luvanga, got crossed up with her goalkeeper at the near post that allowed the ball to sneak past Sandy Maclver.

The Spirit equalized in the ninth minute following a strong run down the left touch line by Trinity Rodman, who then dug out a cross back into the penalty area for an onrushing Sofia Cantore for a tap-in goal.

The second half started with an early Spirit goal following a poor backward pass from Nuria Rábano that was intercepted by Luvanga, the Tanzanian attacker neatly chipping goalkeeper Mandy McGlynn to give Washington the 2-1 lead. The Spirit nearly made it two after Luvanga ran down the left side before crossing the ball into the penalty area with the outside of her boot. Mélissa Bethi scored the tap-in goal, only to be denied by the offside flag that kept the game at 2-1 in favor of Washington.

articles.body: At least one college basketball team is apparently knocking off the rust in the early going of the season. articles.title: Dabo Swinney reacts after Clemson hits latest low with upset loss to Georgia Tech: 'Nobody coming to save us'
articles.summary: Georgia Tech rushed for 269 yards and handed Dabo Swinney one of his worst career losses as Clemson fell 20-6 at home to a team with a losing record.
articles.body: Georgia Tech coach Brent Key overhauled his staff this week, firing multiple assistants amid a four-game losing streak. The shake-up came as a season that began with high expectations spiraled into disappointment. The Yellow Jackets responded Saturday, ending their losing streak with an upset road win over Clemson. The Dabo Swinney coached Tigers managed just 228 total yards in the 20-6 defeat at Memorial Stadium. The loss further dimmed Clemson’s ACC Championship game hopes and left the Tigers with injuries to both quarterbacks. Starter Tait Reynolds was forced to head to the locker room early with a leg injury, and Christopher Vizzina threw for 133 yards and an interception in relief. Vizzina went to the hospital after the game with his own injury. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Swinney reacted to the latest low point in Clemson’s season, acknowledging that any turnaround would have to come from within. "It's difficult, but ain't nobody coming to save us, nobody cares, we've got to find a way to get it done," Swinney said. Clemson has now lost nine of its last 11 home games against Power Four opponents. Under Swinney, the Tigers once put together school-record 40 consecutive home games at Memorial Stadium from 2016 through 2022. "It's frustrating; we've not played well (at home) coming off two really good wins," Swinney continued. "Really expected us to play great today. Great week of practice, but again, it didn't go our way. It's frustrating, but we don't make any excuses. We're not blaming it on injuries. We didn't get it done. It's my job." INDIANA HOOSIERS BOOST COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF HOPES WITH 27-13 WIN OVER USC TROJANS RANKING WHICH POWER 4 COLLEGE FOOTBALL HEAD COACHING JOB IS MOST LIKELY TO COME OPEN NEXT Georgia Tech rushed for 269 yards and two touchdowns. Swinney acknowledged how difficult it is to win when his defense struggles to contain the opposing team's run game. "When you can't stop the run, you don't deserve to win," Swinney said. "But you got to score enough points. We're not doing enough on offense. You don't win the line of scrimmage, you don't deserve to win; they did, give them credit." Swinney’s 7-6 finish in 2025, his worst since 2010, raised questions about his future with the program. A season-opening blowout loss at LSU further intensified scrutiny of his future and renewed attention on the $57 million buyout he would receive if fired this season. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Swinney is owed $60 million beginning in 2027, but a declining buyout schedule would lower Clemson’s obligation to $57 million if he is fired this fall. His contract does not include a mitigation clause, meaning if he lands another coaching job, Clemson would not get a discount on the amount the school owes him. Clemson closes out its ACC regular-season schedule next Friday against Duke. Georgia Tech hosts Wake Forest next week in Atlanta.

articles.title: Florida stuns Kentucky 21-14 as Gators pull off yet another upset win in up-and-down season
articles.summary: Florida Gators pulled off their third upset of a ranked opponent this season, stunning No. 11 Kentucky 21-14 with a gutsy two-point conversion.
articles.body: When you're the No. 11 team in the nation and battling for a crack at the College Football Playoff like the Kentucky Wildcats, you'd normally be licking your chops at the prospect of a 5-4 team paying you a visit. However, that team happened to be the Florida Gators. They've been struggling as of late, but still have a pair of shocking upset wins on their resume this season, taking down both Ole Miss and Texas. So, there was nothing they'd like more than playing spoiler and maybe getting their season back on track. WHICH CURRENT THREE-LOSS TEAM WOULD BE THE MOST DANGEROUS IN THIS YEAR'S COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF? But before we get to the game, we must take a moment to acknowledge Kentucky's drone show. Drones are way better than fireworks. I will die on that hill. Anyway, it took a while for anyone to put points on the board. Kentucky struck first when QB Kenny Minchey found running back CJ Baxter for a touchdown with under two minutes to go in the first quarter. In the second quarter, Florida got rid of its goose egg thanks to an offensive holding penalty in the end zone, which resulted in a safety. As rough as it has been for Florida, they had to have been happy heading to the locker room at halftime trailing just 7-2. And what they had to have liked even more was scoring a touchdown in the third quarter to take their first lead in several weeks. Running back Jadan Baugh took matters into his own hands and punched it into the end zone. Kentucky answered back with a Kenny Minchey 1-yard keeper for a touchdown, while the Gators settled for a field goal to make it 14-13 going into the fourth quarter. Gators quarterback Aaron Philo led the team on an impressive 14-play drive that ended with him using his legs to retake the lead. Jon Sumrall took a bit of a gamble by keeping his offense on the field for a two-point conversion attempt, and that proved to be a good call. Phylo rolled out and lobbed a pass to a wide-open Dallas Wilson to extend the lead to 21-14. But, of course, what would this be without a little drama? Florida decided to go for it on 4th-and-1 just past midfield. A first down would've ended the game as Kentucky was out of timeouts. However, the Wildcats' defense did their job and stopped the Gators about an inch short. That meant the offense got one more crack at it. Unfortunately, for Will Stein's offense, they couldn't get anything going. Minchey threw three straight incomplete passes, then left the offense on the field to go for it on 4th-and-10. The Gators might be the definition of feast or famine this season. That's a third upset win over a ranked opponent... and they're still 6-4 on the year. articles.title: Georgia football three-star recruit Marcellus Young Casario dies after 'medical emergency,' high school says
articles.summary: Marcellus Young Casario, a Georgia Bulldogs defensive lineman commit, died after a sudden medical emergency at his Rabun Gap boarding school.
articles.body: The college football community is mourning the death of a promising young player. Marcellus Young Casario, 18, died Friday after what his high school described as a "sudden medical emergency." Casario was rated a three-star recruit and played defensive line. Casario was from Canada and a senior at Rabun Gap-Nacoochee School, a boarding school in Georgia located roughly 114 miles northeast of Atlanta. The school announced Friday that an unidentified student had died and later postponed a state playoff game scheduled for that night. "The boarding student had a medical incident this morning," the school said in a statement post to social media. "Rabun Gap immediately followed our emergency response protocols, and local emergency personnel responded, transferring the student to the hospital." Casario was later identified as the student. Other details about what led to Friday’s medical emergency were not immediately available. Casario started playing organized football at an independent boarding school in Aurora, Ontario. In 2025 and shortly before his junior season kicked off, Casario transferred to Rabun Gap-Nacoochee. DIVISION-II RUNNING BACK PRONOUNCED DEAD AFTER MEDICAL EMERGENCY IN TEAM'S SEASON OPENER He did see his dreams of receiving a college football scholarship come true. "He was everything a coach wants in a player," Rabun Gap-Nacoochee football coach Derek White said in a statement. He was known for his relentless dedication, and his journey as a student-athlete was marked by hard work and true brotherhood with his teammates." articles.title: Sen-sational turnaround: Lakshya fights back from one game down to lift Kumamoto Masters Japan Open title
articles.summary: India's Lakshya Sen came from a game down to beat Japan's Koki Watanabe in the men's singles final and win the Kumamoto Masters Japan Open title in
articles.body: India's Lakshya Sen came from a game down to beat Japan's Koki Watanabe in the men's singles final and win the Kumamoto Masters Japan Open title in Kumamoto on Sunday.The world No. 13 lost the opening game but fought back to win the next two and seal a 13-21, 21-18, 21-14 victory in one hour and four minutes.Sen took control in the deciding game after opening up a 11-7 lead. He extended his advantage to nine points and did not allow Watanabe to fight his way back into the contest.The title comes shortly after Sen won the Hylo Open in Germany. His victory in Kumamoto also earned him 9,200 ranking points.Watanabe opened up a 3-0 lead, with Lakshya being a tad laid-back initially. The Japanese nailed his smashes to perfection, varying the pace. He repeatedly produced straight down-the-line smashes on Lakshya's forehand side to move to 6-1. Lakshya cut down the lead to 5-8.A judgement error and then a wide return made it 5-10. An angled smash from the Indian was followed by a net error as Watanabe took a five-point advantage into the break.On resumption, Lakshya fought his way back to 10-12, with the Indian producing a straight smash and a defensive block. Another shot going long took Watanabe to a 15-11 lead.Watanabe looked in control as he continued to find winners to establish a six-point lead at 18-12. The Japanese soon grabbed eight game points with another straight return. The Indian saved one before going wide.A change of sides brought a change of fortune as Lakshya surged to a 5-0 lead. The Indian took control of the net and didn't allow his opponent to find his way. He pounced on a loose net shot, and a net error from his opponent helped him maintain his 5-0 lead. A perfect cross-court smash earned him a five-point lead at the break.Despite a few errors, Lakshya's quick racquet speed helped him maintain his lead at 15-10. articles.title: Benches clear in chaotic postgame brawl after Louisville Cardinals top North Carolina Tar Heels
articles.summary: A bench-clearing brawl erupted after Louisville's late interception sealed a 16-14 college football win over Bill Belichick's North Carolina.
articles.body: The Louisville Cardinals managed to beat the North Carolina Tar Heels 16-14 after a late interception ended UNC's hopes of taking the lead. While that sounds exciting, it's no match for the all-out brawl that erupted as the clock wound down to zero. With just over a minute to go, UNC's Travis Burgess seemed to have thrown a pass that would move the Tar Heels close to midfield; however, it wound up in the arms of a Cardinal. RAMS OFFENSIVE LINEMAN PUNCHES BILLS LINEBACKER AFTER THRILLING GAME: 'TEMPERS GOT FLARED' Bummer. That's it. Game over. Everyone can leave. Nothing else to see. Well, any fans who did stick around saw something wild. As the Cardinals took a knee for the final time, tempers started flaring. Then they kept flaring, and really never stopped. The benches cleared, and chaos ensued. We also got one of my favorite things, which is officials trying to break up a brawl by blowing their whistles and throwing flags. Seriously? In that melee, do you really think whistling away like a London Bobby is going to do anything? SEC HEAD GREG SANKEY BLASTS ANNOUNCERS FOR CRITICIZING POOR OFFICIATING IN TEXAS-MISSOURI: 'UNACCEPTABLE' Now you don't just have a brawl on your hands. You have a brawl, a total racket and a bunch of flags you've got to go and pick up. So, did any of that improve the situation in any measurable way? No. No, it did not. Of course, with that much mayhem, there's not much the officiating can do (or would want to do), and it will be interesting to see if there's any supplemental discipline coming. The Tar Heels likely don’t need any, because they’re probably in for a rough few days. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP It was a bad night on several fronts for Bill Belichick's boys. Something tells me it won't be a fun week as the 5-5 Tar Heels prepare to take on Virginia next weekend.

articles.title: ‘El juego por dentro’: Diego Méntrida, campeón de España de triatlón y guía paralímpico, y la mente en una carrera de diez horas

articles.summary: Escúchalo gratis en Spotify, Ivoox, Apple Podcast, Omny, MARCA.com y Radio MARCA
articles.body: MARCA estrena el quinto episodio de la segunda temporada de ‘El Juego por Dentro’ con Diego Méntrida, triatleta, entrenador y guía de triatletas paralímpicos. Campeón de España de larga distancia a finales de octubre en Matalascañas (Huelva) y de media distancia en 2025, es también el triatleta que en el Triatlón de Santander de 2020 esperó a un rival que se había desorientado y le dejó entrar por delante. Méntrida explica cómo se gestiona la cabeza en pruebas de entre ocho y doce horas: "Estás durante esas 8, 10, 12 horas tú solo contra tus pensamientos". Como entrenador, cree que se descuida esa parte: "Solo nos enfocamos en números, en ritmos, en tiempos". Y advierte: "No te sirve nada hacer una preparación por muy buena que sea si no has preparado esa parte mental". Por eso pasa muchas horas entrenando solo, porque eso es lo que vivirá en competición y porque le sirve para "saber cómo eres en tus peores momentos". Esa preparación se la jugó en su primer Ironman, el año pasado en Cozumel (México). En el kilómetro 150 de bici se quedó sin nutrición por haber subestimado lo que iba a consumir. "“No me veía capaz de llegar hasta la segunda transición", recuerda. Ya en ella, sentado y poniéndose las zapatillas, pensó: "Tengo que correr una maratón". Se agarró a que venía con el trabajo hecho y le dio la vuelta. Su temporada 2026 ha sido de lesiones: se fracturó el quinto metatarsiano calentando antes del Campeonato de España de media distancia de duatlón, se rompió un hueso de la mano en una caída en bici y volvió a caerse dos semanas antes del campeonato de larga distancia, que acabó ganando. Sobre lo que supone lesionarse cuando todo gira en torno al deporte, dice: "Sientes que pierdes esa identidad". Y añade: "Se te puede venir el mundo encima si no estás bien acompañado en esos momentos". No vive solo del triatlón, y eso lo vive como una ventaja: “Lo sigo considerando en cierta forma como un hobby". Méntrida habla también de su faceta de guía en el tándem, donde se llega a 55-60 km/h: "La persona que va detrás tiene que confiar plenamente en ti". Estuvo en los Juegos de París 2024 con Jota, ahora acompaña a Héctor Catalá y sueña con Los Ángeles, con una clasificación que va de junio de 2027 a junio de 2028 y solo diez plazas por categoría. Cierra con su hermano Carlos, con síndrome de West, con quien liga toda su trayectoria deportiva y por quien organizó, tras la repercusión de Santander, una carrera virtual solidaria para la fundación de síndrome de West. El Juego por Dentro, el videopodcast de bienestar mental y emocional en el deporte, está disponible en las principales plataformas de podcast (Spotify, Ivoox, Apple Podcast, Omny…) y también en MARCA.com y Radio MARCA. Suscríbete gratis en tu plataforma habitual para no perderte ningún episodio. Mantiene una periodicidad quincenal, con nuevos episodios cada dos semanas en los que deportistas, exdeportistas, psicólogos y expertos en rendimiento comparten su experiencia sobre mentalidad, gestión emocional, presión, liderazgo y crecimiento personal. Una propuesta interesante para profundizar en cómo funciona la mente del deportista y qué hay realmente detrás del rendimiento.

articles.title: De la Fuente denies racism in Spain despite Yamal, Vinicius avowals
articles.summary: Yamal and Vinicius have publicly said they face racist abuse in Spain, which has faced FIFA punishment over the issue.
articles.body:
Weeks after FIFA punished Spain over Islamophobic chants by their supporters and their star Lamine Yamal admitted having repeatedly experienced racism in the country, the Spanish team’s head coach, Luis de la Fuente, has claimed the country does not have a racism problem.

De la Fuente appeared to quash any concerns about racism as he addressed the media on Saturday before his team’s UEFA Nations League match against England .

“In Spain, there is no racism,” the 65-year-old said in response to a question about his England counterpart Thomas Tuchel, who revealed he would speak to his players about the antiracism protocol in place before Sunday’s match in Madrid.

“You can tell this to Thomas. As clear as that. There is no racism. Exactly the same as in England, in Spain, there is no racism. We’re not racists, none of us.”

While a capacity crowd is expected for the top-of-the-table Group C clash at the Metropolitano Stadium, the world champions will have to play their next home friendly with a reduced capacity as a punishment for Spanish supporters singing an Islamophobic chant during a fixture against Egypt in March.

Several high-profile players have been targeted by racist abuse in recent years, including Yamal and Real Madrid’s Brazilian forward Vinicius Jr , who has been moved to tears in news conferences while talking about the issue.

England players faced racist abuse during a game in the Spanish capital in a 2004 friendly in which Black England players, including Ashley Cole and Shaun Wright-Phillips, were targeted.

Tuchel said he did not expect racist abuse on Sunday but his players ⁠⁠would be reminded of antiracism protocols.

“I think the referee and the officials know about that [racist chanting].”

He later clarified his comments as not being specifically about Spain and criticised reporters for creating “a lot of confusion for absolutely nothing”.

“I never talked about racism in Spain. I answered politely a question about what happens,” he said.

England midfielder Declan Rice said the squad knew exactly how to respond if racism occurred.

“In the past, I’ve experienced that in Montenegro, ‌‌Bulgaria, and there was a protocol in place we followed,” Rice told reporters. “We came off the pitch. We know exactly where we are as a group on that.

“I’m not expecting any of that. This is a beautiful city, great stadium. The players we’re playing against we have a lot of respect for. It’s set up to be a really good evening and hopefully not a negative one.”

Yamal has faced racism ‘a thousand times’

In September, Barcelona and Spain star Yamal said he had experienced racism “a thousand ⁠⁠times” with ⁠⁠many people unaware that their comments or behaviour is racist.

Asked by former Argentina international Jorge Valdano in an interview with Spanish broadcaster Movistar whether he had directly experienced racism, Lamine said: “A thousand times.”

“People are indirectly ⁠⁠racist towards you but maybe don’t ⁠⁠realise it. There are a lot of comments or looks that are racist, and they don’t even notice.

“If someone calls me Black, it’s ⁠⁠not going to bother me at all. Ultimately I’m Black. I’m not any other ⁠⁠colour. Another thing is whether it’s ⁠⁠good or bad, whether they’re saying it to offend me.

“But if I’m playing a match. and they paid for a ticket to see ‌‌me, I’m not going to get angry just because they disrespected me.”

Yamal criticised the anti-Muslim chants by fans in what should have been a friendly match against Egypt.

A section of supporters had chanted: “Whoever doesn’t jump is Muslim.”

Egypt’s national anthem also received a barrage of whistles before the friendly.

Yamal, a Muslim whose father moved from Morocco to Spain, issued a damning statement on Instagram in the wake of the row.

“I am a Muslim. Yesterday at the stadium the chant ‘the one who doesn’t jump is the Muslim’ was heard,” he posted.

“I know I was playing for the rival team and it wasn’t something personal against me but as a Muslim person it doesn’t stop being disrespectful and something intolerable.”

Yamal added: “I understand not all fans are like this, but to those who sing these things, using a religion as a mockery on the field makes you ignorant and racist people.”

Real Madrid’s Vinicius has been the most notable target of racism and has openly addressed the issue, often in tearful news conferences.

On May 22, 2023, Vinicius said the Spanish league “now belongs to racists”, and two days later, Spanish police arrested four men suspected of hanging an effigy of him four months earlier from a bridge in Madrid in front of the club’s training centre in advance of a Madrid derby.

The arrests came amid an international outcry after racist abuse was hurled at Vinicius during another league match.

A year later, Vinicius broke down in tears and said he was struggling to stay motivated and enjoy playing football due to the recurring racist abuse he was subjected to in Spain.

During an emotional news conference before Brazil’s friendly against Spain, he expressed frustration that fans kept getting away with hurling racist abuse towards him.

This year, Vinicius praised Yamal for his public condemnation of Islamophobic chants, saying players need to stick together in the fight against discrimination.

“Hopefully, we can continue with this fight,” he said.

“It’s important that Lamine speaks about it. It could help others. We are famous. We have money. We can balance these things better, but the poor people and the Black people who are everywhere, they surely struggle more than we do. So we have to stick together, those who have a stronger voice, the players.”

“I’m not saying that Spain or Germany or Portugal are racist countries, but there are racists in these countries and in Brazil and other countries as well,” Vinicius said. “But if we keep fighting together, I think future players and people in general won’t have to go through this again.”

articles.title: Student strikes gold at Commonwealth karate event
articles.summary: William Jervis, from Grimsby, "proud" after triumphing in the men's Para K22 category.
articles.body:
A student has brought home two gold medals from the Commonwealth Karate Championships.

William Jervis, from Grimsby, represented England at the event in Glasgow.

The 18-year-old won gold in the men's Para K22 category before claiming a second in the club section of the championships.

Jervis, a sports student at Grimsby Institute, said he was "proud" of the achievement, adding: "I've done karate for years and years, I have been doing karate for nine years and I train for six hours a week and do lots."

His medal success comes a year after being selected to represent England at the 2025 Senior European Karate Championships in Armenia.

Mum Clare Jervis said: "I can't tell you how proud we are of William. When he started we didn't expect him to compete, we just expected it to be an activity to do after school, so the medals are a bonus.

"It just shows you what his hard work achieves and he never moans, we travel all over the country to train and he just gets on with it which shows you just how much he loves it. He has great coaches who know how to get the best out of him".

Jervis, who trains at LE Karate in Grimsby, said he competed at the championships in kata – a form of karate in which the athlete must perform a detailed pattern of movements.

The 12th championships took place in Glasgow from 5 to 8 November and brought together competitors from from across Commonwealth nations.

Jonathan Davy, sport programme leader at Grimsby Institute, said: "Everyone at Grimsby Institute is incredibly proud of William and what he has achieved in Glasgow.

"To represent your country at this level is an incredible achievement in itself, but to come home with two gold medals is something really special."

articles.title: Bill Belichick’s UNC Fights Louisville After Injury-Filled Loss
articles.summary: Bill Belichick’s North Carolina Tar Heels didn’t appear to be too happy with losing on Saturday. After the final seconds ticked off the clock against the Lou...
articles.body:
Bill Belichick's North Carolina Tar Heels didn't appear to be too happy with losing on Saturday.

After the final seconds ticked off the clock against the Louisville Cardinals, UNC managed to get involved with fights scattered across the field — not quite a brawl, because things were too spread out, but certainly more postgame feuds than you ever want to see.

At one point, Belichick even got in the mix to try and break things up.

It appears the skirmishes started because of activity on the game's final kneel down.

Louisville offensive lineman Johnnie Brown III kept in contact with North Carolina defensive tackle Xavier Lewis after the final knee.

Their dispute seemed to bring other players in the mix, and soon things were spread out all over the field.

The Associated Press wrote it like this:

"UNC defensive tackle Xavier Lewis and Louisville offensive lineman Johnnie Brown III kept jostling after the kneeldown that would drain the final seconds. That continued and escalated with multiple players stepping in and locking up, as jawing at one other escalated to shoving, players in pileups and a haze of flailing arms with possible punches being thrown. That included multiple skirmishes and at least one tussle that broke off from the main mass of players, leading to a separate pileup of players in an end zone. The teams were eventually separated, with that clean-up work including UNC coach Bill Belichick stepping in to direct and pull multiple Tar Heels players away from the edge of what was brief-but-intense chaos."

North Carolina had just lost frustratingly, 16-14.

There's one on-field view circulating from local reporter Pat Welter.

You can watch it here (or at this link if it doesn't display properly):

As if the loss and the fight weren't bad enough — North Carolina's starting quarterback got hurt.

Billy Edwards Jr. took a big hit on a second-half sack and had to leave the game.

That brought in backup Travis Burgess, who actually made a useful fourth-down throw with 58 seconds left down two points but had the ball deflect unfortunately into the hands of Louisville's Jabari Mack.

That led to the final sequence of knees, which led to the postgame fight — including Belichick trying to stop one of his offensive linemen from getting involved, a bit of a size mismatch

For a North Carolina team that fell to 5-5 (2-4 ACC) with the loss, nothing about this was a sight they'd want to see.

A quarterback injury, a narrow loss and postgame fights? Not a recipe for success at any program.

articles.title: Forget Gibson, Time For Red Wings to Roll With Tarasov
articles.summary: Soon, it would be wise for the Detroit Red Wings to accept that Daniil Tarasov is the best goaltender on […]
articles.body:
Soon, it would be wise for the Detroit Red Wings to accept that Daniil Tarasov is the best goaltender on the roster.

Even after Tarasov stood on his head in a 31-save, 2-0 shutout win that halted Detroit's five-game losing skid, Red Wings coach Todd McLellan wasn't ready to commit to that time being now.

HOW DID THIS STAY OUT 😳 UNREAL save from Daniil Tarasov 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/yZ9D2aSsli — B/R Open Ice (@BR_OpenIce) November 15, 2026

HOW DID THIS STAY OUT 😳 UNREAL save from Daniil Tarasov 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/yZ9D2aSsli

B/R Open Ice (@BR_OpenIce) November 15, 2026

"Well, we've been on the road for 18 of the last 20 some days," was McLellan's response to reporters about whether it was time to go with the hot hand. "We're going to go home, and we're going to relax [Sunday], and we'll take everything into consideration.

"He's obviously played really well, and we believe in him."

At this juncture, there's really only one question to answer.

Gibson is 4-7-1 with a 3.58 goals-against average and .862 save percentage. He's lost his last three decisions and four of his past five.

Gibson ranks 62nd among NHL goalies in GAA. He's 66th overall in save percentage. No NHL netminder who's played at least 600 minutes this season has worse numbers.

In the meantime, the math is adding up to elite numbers for Tarasov. He was signed to be a backup netminder, but he's stopping pucks at an elite level.

In nine appearances, he's 3-3-2. More significantly, among NHL goaltenders, Tarasov is second in save percentage (.931) and third in GAA (1.84).

Daniil Tarasov grabs his second @pepsi shutout as a member of the @DetroitRedWings ! 🐙 What a start to the season he's having! pic.twitter.com/e7rf7aHUF8 — NHL (@NHL) November 15, 2026

Daniil Tarasov grabs his second @pepsi shutout as a member of the @DetroitRedWings ! 🐙 What a start to the season he's having! pic.twitter.com/e7rf7aHUF8

In five of Tarasov's starts, the Red Wings have scored two goals or fewer. Twice, they've not proven capable enough to even get him a goal. And he's managed to be a .500 goalie (2-2-1) in those games, posting two shutouts of his own.

"I'm just trying to be focused on my game, just making the saves," Tarasov said. "Just make the guys' lives easy."

From the outside, it would also seem that Tarasov is making McLellan's decision on who to put between the pipes an easy one.

McLellan appears to be a coach who takes his time to warm up to newcomers. He's quickly embraced Viktor Arvidsson and Andreas Englund , who previously played for him in Los Angeles. He is taking him time to feel that warmth toward Tarasov.

McLellan Says He's Still Learning About Tarasov

"Just learning about him and how he works at his craft," McLellan said. "He's real coachable. I know that. And he's real competitive in practice. He works really hard. Every puck is important to him.

"There's nothing lazy about the rebounds or anything like that. So that's been impressive, and it carries over into his game."

Tarasov has started successive games just once all season, and that was because Gibson was injured . Gibson came into the season as the No. 1 goalie. He's been granted ample opportunity to re-establish his claim to that role and has failed to do so.

The time is overdue for Tarasov to be given the same opportunity. And that opportunity needs to be granted immediately.

articles.title: What Brent Brennan, Noah Fifita and Jay’Vion Cole said after Arizona’s loss to No. 2 Utah
articles.summary: For the third time this season, Arizona found itself neck-and-neck with a ranked opponent late into the game. But like with previous matchups against BYU and...
articles.body:
For the third time this season, Arizona found itself neck-and-neck with a ranked opponent late into the game. But like with previous matchups against BYU and Texas Tech, the Wildcats couldn't come through in the end.

The UA is 7-3 overall, with the three losses by a combined 20 points after falling 40-39 to No. 2 Utah on Saturday night. The defeat ends any consideration of Arizona playing in the Big 12 Conference title game or being part of the 12-game playoff, but the season is far from over.

"I think tonight we showed that we we can play with anybody," UA coach Brent Brennan said. "We're going toe to toe with the No. 2 team in the country, and I don't think there's any doubt about that. And we didn't get it done. The outcome isn't what we wanted, and so now we have 24 hours to learn from it. Because win or lose, 24 hours we got to learn from it."

Arizona visits Kansas State next Saturday and then hosts ASU for the Territorial Cup on Nov. 28. Along with a bowl game, the Wildcats have a chance to record back-to-back seasons of nine or more wins for only the second time in school history and first time since 1974-75.

" y message to the guys after the game was, we got to learn from this and keep moving forward," Brennan said. "We have a lot of good football left to play. This is a great group of young men. They come to work every day. They love each other. They love the U of A, and they're ready. They're going to come back to work tomorrow and be ready to go."

Our game recap can be found here . Below is what Brennan, quarterback Noah Fifita and cornerback Jay'Vion Cole said after the loss:

Brennan on the game atmosphere: "This was an amazing night in Casino Del Sol Stadium. I want to say thank you to our fans, our alums, our students. I mean, that's something that we challenged everybody with all week. And they showed up tonight. They were on their feet all night. It led to four false start penalties for Utah. It was just, it was an awesome atmosphere. And that's something we talk about a lot about, how do we create the best atmosphere in the Big 12, and I thought our fans did that tonight. It was an awesome day on campus."

On the loss: "This was a hard night. This was a heavyweight fight. We said that going into it. We're playing the No. 2 team in the country, and they're good. They're well coached. Coach Scalley does a great job. His staff does a great job. We got a ton of respect for those guys. And to me, this night and the way it went from start, to finish, I think really speaks to just our belief, our resilience, and our response.

"The way our guys responded all night, I thought was really, really special. I thought our defense was making plays. Mays with the fumble recovery, the recovery on the muffed punt, the the incredible interception by Jay'Vion Cole was. I mean the amount of field he had to travel to make that play was just incredible."

On Fifita: "Noah Fifita is one of one. He's special in every way, just the the throws he made, how he stood in there, took shots, how he ran, how tough he is, what a warrior he is, what a leader he is. He is everything that's right about college football and everything that's right about the University of Arizona."

On moving on to the next one: "We got a big time football game on the road at Kansas State, and we dive back into our process. We dive back into Redline. We dive back into the battle of belief and working for each other and putting the work together. And at the end of the day, if we do that, we're going to play good football next weekend on the road at Kansas State."

On the start time getting moved to accommodate Utah's travel delays: "Nothing really changed for us. We were at the benefit of having a home game. They moved the game three hours. Actually, to be honest, I was concerned that it was going to impact our crowd, but it didn't. That was one of the best parts about it, right? You move the game three hours. Our students were there all night on their feet. They never sat down. The fans were on their feet, rocking. It was special. It's awesome. I mean, that's what I'm talking about with the home crowd impact they can have. That's what we need at Casino Del Sol Stadium, and we didn't get it done tonight in the end. But golly, did they impact the whole thing, from start to finish."

On the final offensive play: "We were trying to draw them offside. And that situation right there, that's my fault. I never should have put (center) Zach (Henning) in that position. I never should have put him in that position. We had dummy cadence, so we're trying to get them to jump offside. They moved. They didn't come far enough into the neutral zone. He snapped it, and we didn't have a good answer, so that's my fault."

On receivers Isaiah Mizell and Giovanni Richardson: "Both those guys are studs. They're just awesome players. They come to work every day. They got great attitudes. They got great energy. Coach Wade does a fantastic job coaching them. Att that position, when you have game changers, you're in every game, and that showed up tonight."

On Utah RB Daniel Bray running for 197 yards: "I told you that they have good players, right? That was not a surprise to us, and I think that's probably a little bit of a combination of some missed tackles and him being a good player, and them having good players, and us playing a good football team. We don't want to give up 200 yards rushing, right? So I think we can be better there."

On the offensive line struggling to protect Fifita: "I think we were blocking a good front, and it's hard, and everyone's fighting their ass off, and sometimes you get beat."

Fifita on the loss: "I think naturally, I just kind of think about the plays that I didn't make. Defense gave us the ball back with over two minutes but we didn't do it, so that's the part that kind of hurts. But at the end of the day, gotta live with it and move on to the next."

On Brennan's message after the game: "It's always been about us. Just continue to just love us up and just understand that there's a lot of more football to be played."

On the play calls on the final possession: "I don't think it's my place to kind of speak on that. I'll let kind of the coaches speak on it, but at the end of the day, the ball was in my hands. The play needed to be made, and I didn't make it."

On the crowd and Big Noon Kickoff: "Man, they did a phenomenal job. We appreciate the city. We appreciate the students showing up. They definitely gave us an advantage tonight with that noise and with the energy. I'm just sorry we weren't able to win."

On the focus for the rest of the season: "For us, it's just enjoying every moment with each other. We believe we have a special team still to this day, and enjoying every opportunity and taking advantage of it."

Cole on returning from injury: "It was amazing, being out three weeks and to be out there and compete."

On his interception: "It was crazy. Wasn't supposed to be open, blown coverage and the quarterback threw it up and I was able to get there."

On Utah gaining 500 yards: "They just ran what they ran. We were just undisciplined. We didn't execute."

articles.summary: Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff has been accused of attempting to have a Formula 1 journalist permanently banned from the paddock following a heated confr...
articles.body:
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff has been accused of attempting to have a Formula 1 journalist permanently banned from the paddock following a heated confrontation at the 2023 Las Vegas Grand Prix.

The allegation comes from Jonathan McEvoy, the Daily Mail's long-serving F1 correspondent, whose media accreditation was recently withdrawn by the FIA for the remainder of the 2026 season following a controversial opinion column about Ferrari driver Charles Leclerc.

McEvoy has now revisited an incident involving Wolff three years ago, claiming the Mercedes boss personally approached FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem in an attempt to prevent him from attending another Grand Prix.

The journalist also raised questions about whether his previous disagreements with senior figures in the paddock could have played a role in his latest suspension, although he acknowledged that he had no evidence to support such a connection.

Writing in the Daily Mail, McEvoy recalled his confrontation with Wolff during the inaugural Las Vegas Grand Prix in 2023, when the opening practice session was abandoned after a loose drain cover struck Carlos Sainz's Ferrari.

The incident caused significant disruption to the event, with the Mercedes team principal becoming visibly frustrated when questioned about the potential reputational damage to Formula 1.

Wolff strongly rejected suggestions that the incident had embarrassed the championship, arguing that the situation was being exaggerated.

McEvoy has now claimed that the confrontation continued beyond the press conference, with Wolff allegedly seeking a permanent ban against him.

"He once tried to get me banned from the paddock for life when I asked him a question at the inaugural Las Vegas Grand Prix. He resented my contribution to the press conference and asked Ben Sulayem to stop me from ever attending another race in my life."

According to McEvoy, the FIA president subsequently contacted him during the 2023 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix and offered a revealing assessment of the situation: "The Emirati, a former world rally champion, rang me at the 2023 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, a courtesy I shall remember, and said: 'I don't think Mr Wolff will be sending you a Christmas card this year.'"

The journalist's comments come amid a separate dispute with Formula 1's governing body, which has withdrawn his media accreditation following an opinion piece published after the Mexican Grand Prix.

In that column, McEvoy criticised Leclerc over his opening-lap confrontation with Ferrari teammate Lewis Hamilton, describing the Monegasque as a "sneaky little bastard".

The FIA subsequently informed McEvoy that his article had fallen below the professional standards expected of accredited journalists, resulting in his exclusion from the final three races of the season in Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

McEvoy has suggested that Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur may have influenced the decision, although no evidence has emerged establishing that the Frenchman requested his suspension.

The journalist also questioned whether Wolff could have played a role, referring to the relationship between the Mercedes boss and Vasseur.

"Is this temporary excommunication his revenge? He may not get on as well these days with Vasseur, but they may have rejoined over a mutual enemy (me)," McEvoy wrote.

The Daily Mail has strongly condemned the FIA's decision and announced that it will boycott coverage of the remaining three Grands Prix in response.

articles.title: 5 standout players from Texoma's bi-district high school football playoffs
articles.summary: Brock Belcher made Texas football history, while Brayden Hamill scored six touchdowns. See five Texoma standouts from the bi-district playoffs.
articles.body:
Holliday vs Coahoma UIL high school football playoffs

The opening round of the Texas high school football playoffs delivered record-breaking performances, dominant offensive displays and several memorable moments across Texoma.

Windthorst quarterback Brock Belcher climbed another spot in the Texas high school football record books, while Holliday's Brayden Hamill accounted for six touchdowns in the Eagles' postseason victory.

Henrietta, Graham and Vernon also advanced with convincing wins as area teams began their pursuit of a state championship.

Here are five players who stood out during the bi-district round.

Hamill delivered one of the area's most impressive all-around performances Friday, Nov. 13, accounting for six touchdowns in Holliday's 55-36 victory over Coahoma.

His biggest play came on the first snap of the second half, when he intercepted a pass and returned it for a touchdown, providing an immediate defensive spark for the Eagles.

Hamill's six-touchdown performance helped Holliday pull away from a Coahoma team that entered the postseason with a 7-3 record. The Eagles, who finished the regular season 3-7, scored a season-high 55 points to advance to an area round matchup with undefeated Idalou.

Belcher continued rewriting the Texas high school football record books Thursday, moving into second place on the state's all-time career passing touchdowns list during Windthorst's 61-20 victory over Quanah.

The senior completed 23-of-29 passes for 395 yards and five touchdowns without an interception, adding 59 rushing yards and another score on five carries. His 454 yards of total offense helped the Trojans pile up 603 yards in their playoff opener.

Belcher connected with Aiden Stark for three touchdowns, while Brodie Belz and Elijah Frank caught one apiece. His five touchdown passes brought his career total to 173, moving him past Sunray's Armando Lujan (171) and leaving him behind only Refugio's Travis Quintanilla (186).

Cruse Coleman was nearly unstoppable in Henrietta's 51-point offensive performance in the bi-district round.

The junior running back rushed for 184 yards and four touchdowns on 17 carries, averaging 10.8 yards per attempt. His longest run went for 67 yards, and he accounted for four of the Bearcats' seven touchdowns.

Coleman also made his presence felt defensively, recording 14 tackles, including nine solo stops, to finish as Henrietta's second-leading tackler.

His performance helped power a Bearcats offense that finished with 439 total yards, including 282 on the ground, while showcasing his ability to impact the game on both sides of the ball.

Riley Pratt was a nightmare for opposing offenses in Graham's bi-district playoff opener.

The senior defensive lineman recorded 14 tackles, including 12 solo stops, and finished with five sacks and six tackles for loss. His five sacks accounted for over half of Graham's eight sacks on the night.

Pratt also defended a pass as part of a dominant defensive effort that saw the Steers record 15 tackles for loss, two interceptions and two fumble recoveries.

While Graham's offense piled up 474 yards and seven touchdowns, Pratt's performance on the other side of the ball was just as impressive.

Tyce Payne made his presence felt on both sides of the ball in Vernon's bi-district victory over Ingram Moore.

Payne rushed for 107 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries, averaging 8.9 yards per attempt. He also hauled in a 38-yard reception, finishing with 145 yards of total offense.

The senior was just as productive defensively, recording 11 tackles, including four for loss, along with two quarterback pressures and a sack.

Payne's all-around performance made him one of Vernon's most impactful players, helping move the ball on offense while anchoring a defense that held Ingram Moore to just 167 total yards.
