articles.title: Taking chances and what else Florida football learned from win at UK
articles.summary: What Florida football learned from its win at No 13 Kentucky that it can carry through the rest of the season.
articles.body:
LEXINGTON, Ky. − Florida football took another significant step in its first season under Jon Sumrall with its 21-14 upset win on Saturday, November 14 at No. 13 Kentucky .

The Florida Gators (6-4. 4-4 SEC) picked up their third road win of the season and second road win against a ranked team after knocking off No. 8 Texas 27-24 on October 17 in Austin, Texas.

"I'm trying to win each week," said Sumrall, when asked about winning on the road. "And then the emotions are big every week. Like, I don't care who you play in this league, man. This is a brutal league."

Florida can now clinch its first winning season in the SEC since 2020 when it hosts Vanderbilt in its home finale at The Swamp on Saturday, November 21 (noon, ABC, SEC Network or ESPN).

"it's been a tough October and early November, and a lot of relief," Sumrall siad. "We gotta fight relief syndrome though, and the complacency that comes with a win, because this league, you've seen a lot of people get a win and all of a sudden get relaxed. We've done ourselves some."

Here's what Florida learned from its win over the Wildcats.

Jayden Woods is still capable of being an impact defensive player for Florida football

Woods came up with a big strip sack in the third quarter, recovered by defensive lineman Brendan Bett, that set up UF's first touchdown. The 6-foot-3, 245-pound finished the game with 6 tackles, 2 tackles for loss, 1.5 sacks, 1 forced fumble and 1 pass breakup.

"I just got off the ball, tried to get to the quarterback,:" Woods said. "Of course, (Florida defensive coordinator Brad) White wants us to get the ball off of him, so that was my goal. The other three guys rushing with me up front held him in the pocket for me, guys in the back half covered long enough for me to get there, so shoutout to them."

For the season, Woods has posted 22 tackles and 4.5 sacks.

Florida football coach Jon Sumrall will take chances on special teams

After taking a 10-7 lead early in the third quarter, Sumrall tried an on sides kick to steal a possession against the Wildcats. Kentucky recovered the kick and drove six plays in 45 yards to regain the lead 14-10 with 7:20 left in the third quarter.

Still, Sumrall said he would do it again, given the look Kentucky showed in its kickoff return coverage.

"That was all me with calling the surprise onside kick," Sumrall said. "I've never seen that good of a look for us to hit that kick, and I had already made up my mind after our first offensive touchdown, we're gonna call it. Gotta get that kick a little bit wider."

Florida football plans to experiment with different offensive line combinations

Florida switched center Harrison Moore and right guard T.J. Shanahan in the second quarter, moving Moore to right guard and Shanahan at center. It came after Moore had an errant snap to quarterback Aaron Philo that came close to ending up a turnover.

"After that snap infraction, I just went on the headset, we've worked T.J. plenty at center and felt like we needed to settle ourselves in by making that switch," Sumrall said. "here's some things Harrison actually does better at guard than he does at center. We like him pulling as a guard."

Sumrall also had TJ Dice spell Bryce Lovett at center and Rod Kearney play at both guard spots.

"Some of those guys, we'd like to get more guys reps so we can figure out exactly who they are at times," Sumrall said. "But nobody's playing so much at a high level independently that we don't need to maybe get some other guys shots at times."

Kevin Brockway is The Gainesville Sun's Florida beat writer. Contact him at kbrockway@gannett.com. Follow him on X @KevinBrockwayG1.

articles.title: Ayoub El Kaabi Aiming for January Return; Working Hard
articles.summary: The Moroccan striker’s accelerated recovery from a serious leg fracture offers Olympiacos a vital boost as he battles to rejoin the first team for a grueling...
articles.body:
According to an article by journalist Alexis Virvilis published on the media outlet Gazzetta.gr , Ayoub El Kaabi is recovering well, and if all goes to plan, the Moroccan forward may return to the field with Olympiacos in the coming January at the earliest.

The return of the forward will be very beneficial for Olympiacos as the club are due to enter a tight run of fixtures after the New Year and the January transfer market. The club will be very optimistic about the return of its star striker, and up until now, El Kaabi has not disappointed.

The journalist noted in the article, "What is particularly important in the case of the Moroccan is his response from the very first days after the operation. From the beginning, he showed that he was doing better than the doctors' initial estimates, presenting a very positive picture in the rehabilitation effort."

The article, however, also noted that an injury as serious as a tibia-fibula fracture can never be taken lightly, and treatment cannot be done in a hurry. But, as the journalist noted, El Kaabi looks determined to return as soon as possible. He, as written in the article, has "...a very specific goal: to put on the Olympiacos jersey again and get on the field."

January is the month that the forward has set his sights on as the time when he returns to training with the first team. If he indeed manages to do so, he could start receiving playing time from February itself. However, as Virvilis noted, "Here lies the big challenge. Returning to training is one thing, and being ready for official matches is another. El Kaabi will need time to regain his competitive rhythm, to feel complete confidence in his body and to gain the required intensity."

A return to the field for El Kaabi would mean a great relief for manager Imanol Alguacil, who will then find the services of his best forward at his disposal during one of the most important stretches in the course of a season.

If the Moroccan manages to keep up the pace of his recovery at the current level even after Christmas, a January return would become all the more possible. Motivation looks to be high in the player, and Alexis Virvilis concluded his article with the words, "The goal is not to win a few days, but to definitively win the battle with the injury. And so far, El Kaabi seems to be on a very good path."

articles.body:
The Nebraska Cornhuskers snapped a four-game losing streak on Saturday, defeating the Rutgers Scarlet Knights 31-0. The victory made Nebraska bowl-eligible for the third consecutive season.

Nebraska improved to 8-0 all-time against Rutgers. The 8-0 series edge ties for the most wins without a loss by Nebraska against an FBS opponent.

The Blackshirts posted their first-ever shutout in a Big Ten Conference game. The Huskers had their first shutout since Akron last season.

It was the first shutout in a conference game since 2003 against Iowa State . The defense held Rutgers to 143 total yards and 42 passing yards

The offense had 429 total yards and 237 rushing yards. Nebraska improved to 6-0 on the year when rushing for at least 150 yards.

Nebraska returns next Saturday to host the Ohio State Buckeyes in the home finale; kickoff time is set for 11 a.m. CT.

articles.title: Barry Odom faces harsh reality as Purdue football's losing streak continues
articles.summary: As Purdue football's losing streak continues, the reality is becoming clearer: the Boilermakers might not win another game this season.
articles.body:
IOWA CITY, IOWA — With each week, realization is setting in.

Only now is Purdue football head coach Barry Odom able to absorb a situation he refused to let himself believe was possible.

After No. 15 Iowa's 28-7 victory over the Boilermakers at Kinnick Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, it's more probable than not that Purdue ends the season with six consecutive losses. It's a stunning decline after consecutive wins over Illinois and Minnesota, in a blowout no less, had Purdue sitting at 3-3 at the midway point.

Now, the Boilermakers are staring at its final two games of the 2026 season.

"I know that we've got a coaching staff that is determined to work and pour everything that we've got into it," Odom said. "I know that I've got a locker room full of 80 guys that traveled. I don't doubt their fight at all.

"So, the generalities of fix it, that is pretty wide ranging. If we're just going on wins and losses is what 'fix it' is, I don't know what that reality looks like. But the reality of pouring every single thing into it to continue to move the program forward, we absolutely will do."

Purdue football visits Iowa in primetime | Top photos from the game

Nationwide flight delays and cancellations caused a strategic swerve in Purdue's preparation for Saturday night.

It's not an excuse. Purdue didn't make it one, either. It just was the circumstance the Boilermakers were dealt, boarding four buses for a six-hour route from West Lafayette to Iowa City, arriving late Friday night and having to alter the Saturday schedule leading into arriving at Kinnick Stadium.

This comes five days after Purdue made some tweaks to its defense.

Kevin Kane was fired last Sunday nine games into his second stint as Purdue's defensive coordinator. Dave Steckel, who has coached college football for 37 years, was elevated from senior defensive analyst to Purdue's defensive play caller at Iowa, though Barry Odom said he also did some of the play calling.

Until this season, Steckel been out of it since 2019, the last of his five seasons as Missouri State head coach . Steckel was 13-42 as a head coach. He made a brief return to coaching in 2023 to coach linebackers for the XFL's St. Louis Battlehawks .

"The defense did change a little bit," defensive end Keyshawn Burgos said. "I think everybody really poured into it."

Odom claimed there was defensive progress following Saturday's setback. There were also a few reminders that maybe this whole defensively-flawed team wasn't solely Kane's fault.

Two specific plays, a 44-yard screen play touchdown where Braeden Jackson caught it on the right sideline, reversed field and scored a touchdown just before halftime, looked eerily similar to Maryland's Chris Durr Jr.'s 87-yard score just seven days earlier against Purdue. Xavier Williams' 48-yard touchdown run early in the second half resembled DeJuan Williams' 75-yard score for Maryland a week earlier.

Those plays by Maryland, and an accumulation of many more before them, cost Kane his job.

Now Purdue just has to sit in this one, seeing the same issues arise.

Not just defensively, but offensively, too.

In the first quarter, Evans Chuba relieved Ryan Browne at quarterback.

Well, that was the plan all along, of course.

Purdue had plotted that Chuba, a backup quarterback whose only snaps have come late in blowouts, would be utilized in some short yardage situations. On a third-and-2 late in the first quarter from Purdue's 18, Chuba gained just one yard.

The clock ticked as Odom and offensive coordinator Josh Henson pondered seeing if Chuba could gain at least one more yard on fourth down that would extend the drive. It was all part of a plan Purdue had to try to shorten the game against a heavy favorite.

Instead, Purdue elected to punt rather than risk turning the ball over on downs in an almost no-win situation for the Boilermaker defense.

Instead, it was Iowa who was able to establish a ground game and chew clock, shortening a game that suddenly hurt Purdue.

The Boilermakers rushed for just 99 yards on 28 carries and possessed the ball for less than 25 minutes.

"All I can say is we've got to lock into the small details for this next game," Purdue QB Ryan Browne said. "And it's all things that we know we can do and it's things that we do, but we have to do it more consistently."

How does Purdue correct its current downward trend?

Odom is a determined coach who pours most everything he has into his football program.

He's a firm believer that by outworking the opposition, you're getting a leg up.

The strides made over nearly two full seasons isn't proving Odom's theory.

Purdue has five wins in 22 games under Odom. Only Wisconsin and Indiana remain on the schedule.

Odom will continue to work tirelessly. It's who he is and the only way he knows how to operate.

Now, the stomach punch is that it might not matter in the wins column. Odom doesn't strictly gauge success on wins and losses, but, since we're dealing in reality postgame in Iowa City, that's what the rest of the world uses as a barometer.

Sam King covers sports for the Journal & Courier. Email him at sking@jconline.com and follow him on X and Instagram @samueltking.

articles.title: Rutgers football quarterback situation up in the air for final 2 games
articles.summary: Rutgers football has a murky quarterback situation for the final two games of the season because of injuries.
articles.body:
PISCATAWAY – AJ Surace was only supposed to play in an emergency if Rutgers football needed him against Nebraska.

When third-stringer Sean Ashenfelder suffered an injury early in the first half against the Cornhuskers at SHI Stadium on Saturday, Surace had to come off the sideline and take over.

Coming into the game Surace was listed as a game-time decision.

"I've always had a lot of respect for AJ, but today the toughness he showed" coach Greg Schiano said after his team's 31-0 loss to Nebraska . "AJ played today with three broken ribs."

Not an easy situation to say the least for Surace, who finished 4-of-12 for 24 yards.

It was a tough day all around for Rutgers' offense, which had just 143 total yards of offense, including 101 rushing yards.

Nebraska has a solid defense that ranks among the best in the Big Ten. Going up against a unit like that would be tough enough, let alone trying to do it without Lonergan, star wide receiver KJ Duff and right guard Kobe Asamoah.

"The doctors did a great job and we would never put a guy out there that was at further risk," Schiano said. "But very, very painful. He tried to work through it in practice this week, it was hard. Couldn't do everything. It was hard out there today against that defense."

In an increasingly difficult season, the quarterback situation is only making things more challenging.

And it's not getting any easier with a game against Penn State out at State College on Nov. 21.

Rutgers plays Michigan State, which has also struggled badly this season, in the season finale at SHI Stadium.

Greg Schiano, longtime Rutgers football coach, former NFL coach

Lonergan has missed the last three games due to injury.

Schiano said he didn't have an update on either Surace or Ashenfelder, and he wasn't sure if they'd play in the final two games.

But Surace definitely earned the respect of his teammates trying to fight through three broken ribs.

"Hats off to that kid," center Terrence Salami said. "I've had a bruised rib before, not three broken ribs, and that alone was very painful for me. I have the utmost respect for AJ."

So who Rutgers starts at quarterback going forward remains to be seen.

The situation is getting increasingly unclear with injuries piling up.

"We'll keep fighting, we'll keep figuring it out," Schiano said. "We've got two opportunities left to do it. These kids have busted their tails and we're going to give it everything we've got and tried to help them find a way. Right now the margin of error is very, very thin."

articles.title: New referee announced for Titans-Jaguars Week 10 matchup
articles.summary: NFL officiating crews are being shuffled for Week 10 games after FAA ground stops caused major travel delays.
articles.body:
The NFL and its officiating crews have had a rough season, with controversial calls and questionable rulings so far in 2026, and will face another challenge on Sunday as it shuffles crews because of significant travel delays.

After Friday's historic FAA ground stop crippled air traffic and derailed travel plans, the NFL has adjusted its officiating assignments for Week 10 games, reassigning officials to games within driving distance of their hometowns. As a result, the league is elevating three backup referees for Sunday, including one at Nissan Stadium.

With this change, the Tennessee Titans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars will have a new referee in umpire Barry Anderson, who will be handling the duties for the first time. A longtime official, Anderson worked his way up from side judge in 2007 to field judge in 2011, then to umpire in 2015.

Anderson has been one of the designated backups for officiating crews, with each of the 17 crews having an identified backup referee in every game in case the need arises.

As of this writing, the league has not announced any other changes for the Titans vs. Jaguars, and it appears the rest of the crew is intact.

articles.title: Tottenham reportedly reserve matching right clause to re-sign Kane from Bayern
articles.summary: According to a report by Matt Law in the Telegraph, Tottenham Hotspur still retain an option to re-sign Harry Kane.Even after his recent contract extension w...
articles.body:
According to a report by Matt Law in the Telegraph, Tottenham Hotspur still retain an option to re-sign Harry Kane.

Even after his recent contract extension with Bayern Munich, the London club apparently have a route to sign the Ballon d'Or winner.

The clause is a "matching right", which means that Spurs can match any bid made on Kane should FC Bayern ever decide to sell him.

So, in theory if a club offer a €80million for Kane in 2028, Spurs could match it and Bayern would be legally bound to sell to the latter.

This clause goes back to the original deal and transfer fee negotiated between Bayern Munich and Daniel Levy back in 2023.

However, it's a clause that is likely to end up irrelevant, as every sign indicates that Harry Kane will finish his top level career at Bayern.

articles.title: How life without Cristiano Ronaldo begun with humiliation for Portugal
articles.summary: Portugal 1-4 Denmark: A night of Ronaldo tributes turned sour as Jorge Jesus’ side were routed on home soil
articles.body:
Portugal 's first match since Cristiano Ronaldo's international retirement ended in a ​crushing 4-1 home defeat by Denmark in the Nations League , as a night of tributes in Braga turned sour for Jorge Jesus and his players.

In front of a packed stadium, Portugal's players wore shirts bearing Ronaldo's name and number seven - which has been subject to a redesign to create a lasting legacy for the former captain - during the national anthem.

Supporters unfurled a banner reading "Obrigado, capi7ão", translated to "Thank you, captain", alongside ​images ⁠of him lifting the European Championship and Nations League trophies.

It comes after Ronaldo, 41, called time on his Portugal career on social media last week following a public falling-out with manager Jesus .

Portugal dominated much of the ⁠first half in pouring rain but fell behind shortly before half-time, with Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg converting from the spot after VAR intervened on a handball against Ruben Dias.

Rasmus Hojlund, who had an earlier effort ruled out, doubled Denmark's advantage five minutes ‌after the interval, slipping behind the defence to meet a cross from ‌the right with a powerful volley.

The striker scored again seven minutes later, cutting inside Renato Veiga on a counter-attack before firing a right-footed shot past Diogo Costa from the edge of the box.

Andersen completed the rout in the 75th minute, rising to power home a towering ⁠header from inside the area after Mathias Jensen delivered a free kick from the right.

Bernardo Silva scored a consolation goal for Portugal three minutes into added time, firing home from close range after the goalkeeper parried the ball.

"Practically everything went wrong for us... It's actually hard to find an explanation," midfielder Joao Palhinha told Portuguese broadcaster Sport TV.

"It was an unlucky night for us; we made it far too easy for our opponents. We've got a match on Tuesday, so weve got until then to reflect about what happened today. But I have no doubt whatsoever that we'll bounce back and secure top spot in the group in Wales."

Norway beat Wales 3-1 in Oslo in the other League A Group Four match, with Antonio Nusa and Andreas Schjelderup scoring before Erling Haaland's late penalty sealed victory.

Portugal remain top on 12 points, three ahead of Denmark, with Norway third on six and Wales bottom on three.

One round of group-stage matches remains, with Wales hosting Portugal and Denmark at home to Norway on Tuesday.

articles.title: Auston Trusty nets on first appearance since losing his dad
articles.summary: Celtic defender Auston Trusty made his first appearance since the death of his father, and scored his second goal for his country in the USA’s thumping 6-0 v...
articles.body:
Celtic defender Auston Trusty made his first appearance since the death of his father, and scored his second goal for his country in the USA's thumping 6-0 victory over Haiti in the first leg of the Concacaf Nations League quarter final in Miami…

Auston Trusty of United States scores his team's first goal during the CONCACAF Nations League Quarterfinal match between Haiti and United States at Nu Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Miami, Florida. (Photo by JC Ruiz/Getty Images)

Celtic has given Auston all the time that he needs

The towering centre half hasn't featured for the Hoops since his father Walt passed away, with Celtic giving him all the team that he needs to grieve for his dad and to be with his family at this sad time. Some things are more important than football.

Trusty was recently on the receiving end of some ill advised comments from former Celtic hero Frank McAvennie regarding his absence, despite it being well known that he was grieving the loss of his father. Frank has subsequently apologised for his insensitive remarks.

Folarin Balogun #20 of United States celebrates scoring his team's sixth goal with teammate Auston Trusty during the CONCACAF Nations League Quarter final match between Haiti and United States at Nu Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Miami, Florida. (Photo by JC Ruiz/Getty Images)

Trusty returned to action for United States

The 28 year old Celtic defender returned to action after being called up for international duty for the USA's games against Haiti in the Concacaf Nations league.

Trusty has scored just 11 career goals and his last effort for the hoops was in a Celtic Park Europa league clash against Utrecht at the start of 2026, although he did find the net for his country in the hosts World Cup finals clash with Turkey back in the summer.

The 28-year-old connected with a Sebastian Berhalter delivery in the tenth minute.

Trusty showed a strikers instinct as he timed his run and the finish to perfection to side-foot the ball home from six yards out much to the delight of the supporters at the packed Nu Stadium in Miami.

Later, in the second half, Julian Hall doubled the USA's lead.

Auston Trusty of United States celebrates scoring his team's first goal with teammates during the CONCACAF Nations League Quarterfinal match between Haiti and United States at Nu Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Miami, Florida. (Photo by JC Ruiz/Getty Images)

AC Milan's Christian Pulisic then scored two goals in the space of as many minutes to put the Stars and Stripes on easy street rendering the return leg at TQL Stadium in Cincinnati as nothing more than a mere formality.

An emotional post-match interview on TNT Sports

After the match the Celtic defender was interviewed pitch-side by Melissa Ortiz on TNT Sports who congratulated him on the win and for his second international goal. She continued: "After everything you've been through in the past month, ho meaning was tonight for you in scoring a goal?"

Auston replied: "Very meaningful, I'm trying not to cry. My dad passed away not so long ago, so to come out here and win…this is my first time playing the game since he passed, so I dedicate the goal to him."

Auston could possibly feature for his national side on Wednesday night, before heading back to Scotland where he will meet up with his club teammates for the first time in a month.

Martin O'Neill will naturally be delighted to see the former Arsenal and Sheffield United back as it will give him some much needed options in the centre of the defence.

Auston could be involved next weekend for the visit of St Mirren to Celtic Park and he is sure to get a warm reception from the Celtic support. Playing for the United States will also help the Celtic central defender with match fitness ahead of a crucial run of games for Celtic over the next few weeks.

The Texas A&M football program is going through one of its most challenging spells, with results not coming and questions being raised about players and coaches.

The latest defeat to Tennessee has resulted in a 4-6 record for Mike Elko's team and further brought up QB Marcel Reed as a topic of discussion.

Elko tried to blame the entire offense and himself rather than just Marcel Reed.

"Our offense inept. I don't know how you can put this on one kid. This is not on one kid. The narrative that this is just on Marcel — anybody who watched that game and thinks it's just on Marcel Reed — it's on me. It's on me," he said via Carter Karels' X .

While Mike Elko tried his best to protect his QB1, the fact that he threw for just 71 yards with no touchdowns and one interception made fans question the head coach, with one fan saying "mostly his fault but the OC is also terrible".

Mike Elko Issues Apology to Fans After Loss

The defeat to Tennessee further exposed Texas A&M's offensive frailties, and Elko was deeply apologetic to the fanbase after yet another poor display.

"Utter apology with everything that I have to everybody that supports this program. Thank you for turning out; you deserve so much better," he said postgame via On3's X.

Elko also asked for another opportunity to make things right.

"Give me a chance, and we will get this fixed and put a much better product on the field. That's all I can say." After calling the offensive performance "pathetic", Elko further explained how wind played a role as well.

"The wind played a role. The rush played a role. Our inability to give him any time to see anything. They're very multiple on defense, so the pressure created a massive challenge trying to do anything."

The Aggies take on the Oklahoma Sooners next on Saturday.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino hails 'amazing future' for USMNT as he prepares for Manchester United move after Haiti rout
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino has backed the USMNT to achieve greatness on the international stage after his side dismantled Haiti in a dominant 6-0 victory. The Argen...
articles.body:
Mauricio Pochettino has backed the USMNT to achieve greatness on the international stage after his side dismantled Haiti in a dominant 6-0 victory. The Argentine tactician is set to leave his post to take over at Manchester United, but he insists he is leaving behind a squad capable of competing at the highest level.

Clinical second-half display seals dominant victory in Miami

Auston Trusty scored from a 10th-minute corner before the United States fired five goals after the interval against nominal hosts Haiti in South Florida, where violence in the Caribbean nation prevented Les Grenadiers from playing at home. Making his first international appearance since the World Cup, Christian Pulisic struck twice in two minutes to reach 35 goals in 91 caps, surpassing Eric Wynalda for fourth on the all-time scoring chart.

Weston McKennie, substitute Folarin Balogun, and teenager Julian Hall - who officially cap-tied himself to the U.S. over Poland with his fourth goal in five appearances - completed the rout. A largely pro-Haitian crowd briefly roared in the 70th minute when Lenny Joseph finished Josue Casimir's cross, only for the offside flag to rule out the effort.

Pochettino praises squad professionalism ahead of Old Trafford move

Having confirmed on Friday that he will depart to Manchester United just three months into a new four-year contract, Pochettino lauded his players' focus during the biggest victory of his two-year tenure.

"They were very, very professional from the day one when they started to see all the rumors and then when we confirmed it a few days ago," Pochettino told reporters. "And I think if you say to me, what we feel proud of, we feel so proud of the players and how they manage the situation in a mature way."

AC Milan attacker Pulisic echoed that forward-looking mindset while wishing his outgoing manager well at Old Trafford. "I think he has a big opportunity there and yeah, we just have to continue as we're doing and try to continue to grow as a team," Pulisic said. "I think we had some good moments, and he brought a lot of excitement to the team. So I think he'll leave that behind."

Strong foundations left in place for incoming USMNT leadership

Saturday's landslide makes Tuesday's Nations League quarter-final second leg in Cincinnati a formality, with Pochettino confident the blend of youth and experience guarantees sustained progress.

"I think we have an amazing future, brilliant future in this country with the national team," Pochettino said. "I think if we want to go for big things, that is in the way of the construction of the structure and the principles I think are here now and it's only continuing.

"In the last two years, the kids, the young kids that appear and you can see how they play very relaxed because of what the experienced players provide, that platform to perform."

Liverpool test awaits Pochettino as USMNT turn to interim leadership

Following Tuesday's return fixture against Haiti, Pochettino officially starts at Manchester United on November 18 ahead of a daunting Anfield clash against Liverpool on November 22. Meanwhile, Under-23 coach Steve Cherundolo will oversee the USMNT's December training camp while officials appoint a yet-to-be-named permanent successor before March's Nations League semi-finals and final.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino’s exciting starting XI that will rocket Man United up the table
articles.summary: Manchester United have appointed Mauricio Pochettino as the new head coach of the club.Mauricio PochettinoHe will be the eighth man charged with trying to ta...
articles.body:
Manchester United have appointed Mauricio Pochettino as the new head coach of the club.

He will be the eighth man charged with trying to take the club back to the dizzying heights of times under Sir Alex Ferguson.

The Argentine coach will likely have his own ideas on how to get his United squad there and will surely have targets in the transfer market.

Here is who Pochettino will count on for United's squad.

Senne Lammens will undoubtedly be the starting keeper for the club and Pochettino will hope to restore the Belgian to his form during the 2025/26 season.

Full-back has been a much bigger problem for the Red Devils in recent years and it is far from clear what Pochettino will do.

Diogo Dalot has often been the starting full-back under Michael Carrick, but Pochettino requires attacking quality in the final third from his right- and left-backs. For that reason, Amad might see a return to a defensive position, while Patrick Dorgu may consolidate his place as left-back.

The Dane has much more energy and attacking intent than Luke Shaw at this stage of his career and seems the logical choice.

Leny Yoro will be necessary in the United defence as Pochettino plays a high line and United will need Yoro's recovery speed. Lisandro Martínez may also be trusted more by his compatriot, and his ball-playing ability and physicality will be required.

The midfield will also raise numerous questions. One player whom Pochettino will probably love, when fit, is Carlos Baleba, who can play a screening role and cover ground.

Kobbie Mainoo and Bruno Fernandes will likely make up the final two spots in midfield owing to their reputation in the squad and their ability to influence the game when on top form.

The front three appear to be pretty straightforward when they are fit. Matheus Cunha should shine in a between-the-lines role and Bryan Mbeumo's speed and ability to finish will be appreciated.

What's more, both wingers are willing pressers, and that is also why Benjamin Šeško should be a strong candidate to play numerous games for Pochettino. His physicality and willingness to run and press will be lapped up by the Argentine.

articles.title: ❌ Luis de la Fuente's four omissions for Spain-England

articles.body:
Luis de la Fuente has named his final 23-man squad for tonight's match against England at the Metropolitano. To finalise the official squad, the Spain coach has left out Álvaro Valles, Jacobo Ramón, Jorge de Frutos and Roberto Fernández for tactical reasons.

The decision is mainly down to the return of key players in attack and defence, including Lamine Yamal, Mikel Oyarzabal, Nico Williams and Aymeric Laporte. With these big names back in the fold, the coach from La Rioja has had to trim his options up front and at the back.

Roberto Fernández and Jorge de Frutos both miss out despite having featured in the previous match against the Czech Republic in Prague. Meanwhile, goalkeeper Álvaro Valles and centre-back Jacobo Ramón, both new additions for this international window, will also watch the match from the stands.

These four tactical omissions come on top of the previously confirmed absence of Álex Grimaldo, who left the Spain camp with flu. This completes the five changes the coaching staff needed to make to the initial squad for the final match of the Nations League group stage.

With their place in the quarter-finals already secured, Spain will be aiming for at least a draw against Thomas Tuchel's side when the match kicks off at 20:45. That result would be enough for La Roja to clinch top spot in their group in front of their home fans.
